Role Title: AI Conversation Evaluator

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote – Global (English required)


Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: $45–70/hour

Time commitment: Approximately 7.5 hours total

Project kickoff: Sunday, November 15

Project duration: Short-term project, expected to run through November 18

You'll need: An active personal ChatGPT account (Free or Plus), access to a computer or smartphone, and availability during the project window.

Your tasks: Interact with different versions of an AI assistant through everyday conversations, compare the overall experience, and provide structured ratings and brief written feedback.


About the role

AI assistants are becoming part of everyday life, helping people with everything from writing emails and planning trips to answering questions and solving problems. We want to understand how natural, helpful, and enjoyable these interactions feel from the perspective of real users. That's where you come in.

You'll test different AI experiences using your own ChatGPT account, engage in everyday conversations, and share your feedback on what worked, what didn't, and which experience you preferred.


What you'll do

  1. Engage in a series of natural, multi-turn conversations with different AI assistants.
  2. Use everyday scenarios such as writing, planning, researching, brainstorming, or asking questions.
  3. Compare AI responses and select your preferred experience.
  4. Evaluate conversational quality, helpfulness, clarity, tone, and overall user satisfaction.
  5. Identify behaviors that feel unnatural, repetitive, or unnecessary.
  6. Provide short written feedback highlighting positive and negative moments.
  7. Follow simple testing guidelines and document your evaluations accurately.


Who we're looking for

  1. Active ChatGPT user, using the platform at least 3 times per week.
  2. Must have a personal ChatGPT Free or Plus account.
  3. Comfortable interacting with AI assistants for everyday tasks.
  4. Detail-oriented, with the ability to follow instructions and provide thoughtful feedback.
  5. Clear written communication skills; English proficiency preferred.
  6. Available to participate between November 15–18.
  7. Generalists welcome; no specific professional background required.
  8. No coding or previous AI evaluation experience needed.


Why you'll like it

  1. Get paid to use and evaluate AI tools you're already familiar with.
  2. Work remotely, with flexibility during the project window.
  3. Participate in a short-term project with competitive hourly compensation.
  4. Have a direct impact on improving the quality and user experience of conversational AI.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply: Submit your application and confirm your availability.
  2. Complete the screening questions: Share your ChatGPT usage frequency and account type (Free or Plus).
  3. Interview: A short interview, if required, to confirm your eligibility.
  4. Profile review: If everything looks good, we present your profile to the client.
  5. Onboarding: Our Talent Ops team will contact you with instructions to get started.

Role Title: Software Engineer - Backend


Role Type: Contractor (~15 hrs a week)


Location: Remote


You’ll create Reinforcement Learning Environments that test a model’s ability to solve real software engineering problems: tracking down subtle bugs, building non-trivial features, refactoring, and optimizing performance. Each task means defining the problem, building a reproducible environment, and writing a reference solution.


Scope of Work

  1. Create realistic, challenging coding tasks for frontier AI models, drawn from repositories you know well.
  2. Design problems that require real engineering skill — subtle bugs, non-trivial features, meaningful performance work — not lookup or boilerplate.
  3. Build a reproducible environment for each task.
  4. Write deterministic verifiers that accept correct solutions across different valid implementations, while rejecting incorrect, incomplete, or hard-coded approaches.
  5. Provide a reference solution showing how the task can be solved.
  6. Flag tasks that turn out to be ambiguous or unverifiable rather than submitting them.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Significant hands-on expertise in at least one of: Python3, Java, Rust, Go, C++, or TypeScript.
  2. Deep understanding of algorithms, data structures, and software engineering principles.
  3. Proven ability to debug complex systems, resolve bugs, and deliver effective optimizations.
  4. Experience with large codebase refactoring and legacy system modernization.
  5. Track record of delivering high-impact features from conception through delivery.
  6. Strong documentation and communication skills to articulate technical concepts clearly.
  7. Interest in AI and its technical challenges — previous AI experience not required.


Compensation Structure

Compensation is output-based; experts are paid per task that meets the project specifications. The time required may vary depending on your experience and workflow.


Start Timeline & Availability

We typically fill roles within 48 hours and are looking for experts ready to jump in right away. If selected, we expect you to start your first tasks within 24–48 hours of completing onboarding.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions
  2. Complete the AI interview for this role — it’s how your expertise gets in front of the client
  3. Profile review
  4. Onboarding — our Talent Ops team will get you set up

Job Title: Competitive Coder

Job Type: Contractor (15hrs+ a week)

Location: Remote


Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: $30 - $100

Commitment: 15+ hours per week

Location: Fully remote

You’ll need: Strong competitive programming background and advanced C++

Your tasks: Create original competitive programming problems with reference solutions and robust test suites


You’ll create Reinforcement Learning Environments that test a model’s ability to solve hard algorithmic problems. Each task means writing an original problem that doesn’t exist on any online judge, a correct reference solution, and a test suite strong enough that a wrong solution fails.


What you’ll do

  1. Design original competitive programming problems, absent from Codeforces, AtCoder, and all other judges.
  2. Write a correct reference solution and verify it against the constraints.
  3. Build a robust test suite: edge cases, maximum constraints, and tests that break plausible wrong approaches.
  4. Implement checkers for problems with multiple valid outputs.
  5. Document the problem’s intended solution, complexity, and the reasoning behind your test cases.
  6. Review problems from other contributors for correctness and test coverage.
  7. Flag problems that turn out to be ambiguous or have unintended solutions.

What we’re looking for

  1. Strong competitive programming record — Codeforces, AtCoder, ICPC, IOI, or equivalent.
  2. Advanced C++ for reference solutions and checkers.
  3. Deep algorithmic knowledge and the ability to reason about constraints, complexity, and edge cases.
  4. Meticulous attention to detail in validation and output consistency.
  5. Clear written and verbal English for documenting problems and edge cases.
  6. Comfortable working independently and meeting deadlines.
  7. Prior experience as a problem setter, tester, or checker on a major platform is a strong plus.


Compensation Structure

Compensation is output-based; experts are paid per task that meets the project specifications. The time required may vary depending on your experience and workflow. Minimum submission requirements apply.


Start Timeline & Availability

We typically fill roles within 48 hours and are looking for experts ready to jump in right away. If selected, we expect you to start your first tasks within 24–48 hours of completing onboarding.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions
  2. Complete the AI interview for this role — it’s how your expertise gets in front of the client
  3. Profile review
  4. Onboarding — our Talent Ops team will get you set up

Role Title: Finance Research Expert


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: $30 - $60 per hour

Time per task: around 4 to 8 hours

Location: Remote, worldwide

You’ll need: Hands-on experience reading US SEC filings and familiarity with US GAAP

Your tasks: Write finance research questions with a verified, sourced answer, and check each one against what AI models answer


Scope of Work

You will work on questions about real US public companies. Each question points to information that sits in long filings or IR materials, or that requires comparing several of them to find the right answer.


  1. Write questions that require finding a specific figure in a 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, proxy statement, earnings release or investor presentation.
  2. Write questions where two documents show different numbers and the answer depends on knowing which one is correct (for example, original vs. restated figures, or adjusted vs. reported).
  3. Pay attention to period and document version: the right fiscal year, the right filing, the latest amended version.
  4. Test each question against current AI models and keep only the ones they answer incorrectly.
  5. Rewrite questions when the wording allows more than one valid answer.


What we’re looking for

Hands-on work with US filings in one of these backgrounds:

  1. Equity research or investment analysis (sell-side or buy-side) covering US companies.
  2. Investment banking or corporate development (M&A, equity capital markets), with experience in deal filings, prospectuses, ownership history and subsidiary structures.
  3. Credit or restructuring analysis, with experience in credit agreements, bond terms and bankruptcy filings.
  4. SEC reporting or audit (Big 4 audit, corporate reporting), with experience in restatements, footnotes and how figures change across filings.
  5. Corporate law or due diligence (securities law, KYC, investigations), with experience tracing entities, executives and related parties across records.


You should also be comfortable reading long filings, including footnotes and tables, and have clear written English.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply with your resume and a short profile.
  2. Complete the finance interview. It is a short conversation about your experience with US filings and financial reporting. You don’t need to prepare or write anything. Finishing it is what moves your application forward.
  3. Review. We check your experience against what the project needs.
  4. Onboarding and first task. If selected, you get the guidelines and start with an initial task, which is reviewed before you continue.

Role Title: Music & Sound Annotation Expert


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


micro1 is engaging Music & Sound Annotation Experts to contribute to a customer's project at the forefront of music and audio technology.

Your ears are the ground truth. You'll listen to short field recordings and document exactly what's audible — instruments, tempo, key, background sounds, crowd reactions — through a structured web platform built for this project. Later phases involve grading AI model answers against what you actually heard.


What you'll do

  1. Listen to 30–90 second field recordings (headphones, your own quiet workspace) and complete structured annotations: which instruments are present, tempo and key, timestamps of background events (traffic, sirens, applause), scene details
  2. Compare paired recordings of the same song captured at different locations and judge what stayed the same and what changed
  3. In later phases: review AI model descriptions of clips and mark what's correct, wrong, or invented, with a brief written explanation
  4. Attend a paid onboarding/calibration session and a short weekly sync


Who we're looking for (any of these backgrounds)

  1. Working or gigging musicians, session players, producers, or mixing engineers
  2. Music educators, ear-training instructors, band/choir directors, conservatory students or graduates
  3. Location sound recordists, sound designers, foley artists, or podcast/documentary audio editors


Requirements

  1. 3+ years of hands-on music or audio experience
  2. Strong analytical listening: you can pick individual instruments out of a busy, noisy, real-world mix — not just studio recordings
  3. Can identify tempo (within a few BPM) and musical key (relative pitch with a reference is fine)
  4. Comfortable with detail-oriented, repetitive annotation work in a web platform — dropdowns, timestamps, short structured notes
  5. Clear written English for brief, evidence-based notes (e.g., "accordion enters around 0:12")
  6. Quality headphones, quiet workspace, reliable internet
  7. Available 20–25 hrs/week for the engagement window

Role Title: Principal Engineer / Professor — Technical Expert


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


Opportunity Snapshot

Pay: $80- $185/hour

Commitment: Flexible — fits alongside your current role

Location: Fully remote

You’ll need: Master’s or PhD in an engineering or physical science field, plus principal-level industry experience or a faculty appointment

Your tasks: Build challenging technical problems from your own domain and define what makes an answer correct


micro1 is engaging principal-level engineers, scientists, and faculty to design the technical problems that measure what AI systems can actually do. Your domain expertise is what matters here — no prior AI experience required.


We’re building this across four areas: aerospace, semiconductors, manufacturing and industrial engineering, and materials science. If your work sits in one of those — or across two of them — this is for you.


The work draws on what you already know: the problems where the textbook answer isn’t enough, where the right approach depends on reading the constraints correctly, where a plausible-looking solution is quietly wrong.


What you’ll do

  1. Design difficult technical problems from your own area, with realistic constraints and supporting data.
  2. Provide the correct solution and walk through the reasoning that gets there.
  3. Define objective criteria for correctness, so another expert reviewing the work would reach the same verdict.
  4. Review problems built by other contributors for technical accuracy and soundness of method.
  5. Flag problems that turn out to be ambiguous or ungradable rather than submitting them.

What we’re looking for

  1. Master’s or PhD in engineering, physics, materials, or a closely related field.
  2. Principal, staff, or fellow-level experience at a major engineering organization, a national lab, or a faculty appointment at a leading university.
  3. Deep technical depth in at least one area, with hands-on ownership of the work.
  4. Able to explain why an answer is correct clearly enough that another expert could verify it.
  5. Publications, patents, or a record of technical leadership is a strong plus.

How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions
  2. Complete the AI interview for this role
  3. Profile review
  4. Onboarding — our Talent Ops team will get you set up

Role Title: Bluebook Citation Specialist (Law Students & Recent JDs)


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


Opportunity Snapshot


Pay: $50–80/hour

You’ll need: Current or recent law school enrollment, hands-on Bluebook experience, and law journal or law review editing experience

Your tasks: Review citation-checking rubrics and build sample cite-checking tasks


Job Description

micro1 is engaging law students and recent law graduates with law journal experience to support a legal citation project. If you’ve spent time cite-checking for a law review or journal, this is that skill applied to a new context. No prior AI experience is required — your Bluebook fluency and editorial judgment are what matter.


Scope of Work

  1. Review existing Bluebook and pincite grading rubrics, and flag rules that are unclear, incomplete, or would be applied inconsistently by different editors.
  2. Identify edge cases the rubrics don’t currently cover and recommend how they should be handled.
  3. Create sample cite-checking tasks: source material paired with citations containing realistic errors, along with the correct answer and an explanation of the rule involved.
  4. Build tasks across a range of citation types and difficulty levels, from straightforward formatting errors to subtle pincite and source-support problems.
  5. Apply Bluebook rules consistently across all submissions.
  6. Flag ambiguous cases to project coordinators instead of resolving them silently.
  7. Deliver assigned work on schedule and at the required quality level.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Current law student (2L, 3L) or recent JD graduate.
  2. Law review or law journal experience, ideally including a cite-checking or source-collection role.
  3. Strong working knowledge of The Bluebook, including pincites, short forms, signals, and parentheticals.
  4. Able to explain why a citation is wrong, not just that it is — the reasoning matters as much as the correction.
  5. Careful and consistent across long sessions of detailed review work.
  6. Comfortable working independently and meeting deadlines without close supervision.
  7. Experience as a journal editor, articles editor, or executive editor is a plus.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions
  2. Complete the AI interview— this is how we showcase your skills to the client
  3. Profile review by the hiring team
  4. Onboarding — our Talent Ops team will get you set up

descriptions.236aada3-b184-4ba5-88d2-a3de031ed1bd:
Job Title: VP of Robotics Research


Job Type: Full-time


Location: Remote


The Role

As VP of Robotics Research at micro1, you will define and lead our research agenda for Physical AI — intelligent systems that can understand, reason about, and act in the physical world.


Our research focuses on four connected areas:

  1. Physical Agents & Robotics — building agents that perceive, reason, plan, and act through robots, machines, instruments, and other physical systems.
  2. Learning & Data — studying how demonstrations, trajectories, sensor data, simulation, feedback, and autonomous experience improve physical-world intelligence.
  3. Evaluation & Generalization — developing rigorous methods to measure physical reasoning, manipulation, planning, robustness, safety, and transfer across tasks and environments.
  4. Physical-World R&D Automation — exploring how agents can accelerate scientific and engineering workflows through simulation, experimentation, design, fabrication, and real-world tools.


You will set research direction across these areas, stay close to models and physical systems, build a world-class research team, and partner with leading AI and robotics labs on their hardest Physical AI problems.


What You’ll Do

  1. Set the Physical AI research agenda. Identify the highest-leverage problems across robotics, embodied agents, learning, data, evaluation, and physical-world automation.
  2. Build agents that act in the physical world. Develop systems that connect foundation models and agents to robots, machines, instruments, and other physical interfaces.
  3. Advance general-purpose robot learning. Lead research across vision-language-action models, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, world models, and multimodal policies.
  4. Develop a science of physical-world data. Study which demonstrations, trajectories, sensor streams, environments, and supervision signals best improve learning and generalization.
  5. Build scalable data-generation systems. Develop methods for generating high-quality interaction data through human demonstration, teleoperation, autonomous rollout, simulation, and hybrid human–agent workflows.
  6. Advance evaluation and generalization. Build rigorous benchmarks for manipulation, spatial reasoning, planning, tool use, robustness, safety, and transfer across tasks and embodiments.
  7. Bridge simulation and reality. Study how simulated and real-world experience should be combined and where sim-to-real transfer breaks down.
  8. Advance physical-world R&D automation. Build agents that operate across scientific and engineering workflows, including simulation, experimentation, design, fabrication, and laboratory systems.
  9. Build research that compounds. Create reusable datasets, environments, simulators, hardware testbeds, evaluation infrastructure, and research tools.
  10. Build and lead the research team. Recruit and develop exceptional researchers and engineers, partner with leading labs, and publish consequential research.


What We’re Looking For

  1. Deep Physical AI expertise. Significant experience in robotics, embodied AI, robot learning, autonomous systems, or related fields.
  2. Strong learning and agentic systems intuition. Deep understanding of modern robot learning, multimodal models, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, world models, planning, and control.
  3. Physical systems intuition. Strong understanding of sensing, calibration, control, contact, actuation, latency, uncertainty, and hardware constraints.
  4. Exceptional research taste. You identify problems that can meaningfully expand what AI systems can do in the physical world.
  5. Experimental rigor. You turn open questions into strong hypotheses, controlled experiments, meaningful baselines, and evidence-backed conclusions.
  6. Strong evaluation judgment. You understand generalization, distribution shift, benchmark design, hardware-specific effects, and the failure modes of physical AI evaluations.
  7. Systems thinking. You reason across models, agents, data, hardware, simulation, tools, and evaluation as parts of a single system.
  8. Technical range. You are comfortable moving between model training, agent design, simulation, evaluation infrastructure, and physical experimentation.
  9. Research leadership. You have experience setting direction, mentoring exceptional technical talent, and leading ambitious research programs under uncertainty.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Master’s or PhD in Robotics, Computer Science, AI, Machine Learning, Engineering, or a related field.
  2. Research experience at a leading AI, robotics, or embodied intelligence organization.
  3. Strong publication record at venues such as CoRL, RSS, ICRA, IROS, NeurIPS, ICML, or CVPR, or equivalent high-impact technical work.
  4. Experience with generalist robot policies, cross-embodiment learning, robot foundation models, or large-scale imitation and reinforcement learning.
  5. Hands-on experience with robotic platforms and frameworks such as ROS/ROS2, Isaac Lab, MuJoCo, ManiSkill, or equivalent systems.
  6. Experience building robotics benchmarks, simulation environments, teleoperation systems, safety evaluations, or physical-world data engines.
  7. Experience building agents for engineering, scientific, manufacturing, or laboratory workflows.


Compensation & Benefits Notice

The national pay range for this full-time position is base salary of $250,000 –$350,000. All employees are eligible for equity compensation, and employees may also receive performance-based bonuses, dependent on role and subject to company policies. micro1 provides a comprehensive benefits package, including up to 100% reimbursement for health-insurance premiums, paid time off, a 401(K) plan with a company match, and additional benefits designed to support a high-performing, remote-first workforce.


micro1 is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, or gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable local laws, regulations and ordinances. If you need assistance and/or a reasonable accommodation during the application process, reach out to support@micro1.ai.

descriptions.14883aba-fc23-4ca4-8935-9d8d72794668:
Role Title: Small/Medium Business – Robotics Data Collection Partner


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


micro1 is looking for small to medium business owners who want to participate in a paid video data collection project for AI.


Your business would help collect real videos of normal work happening in your workplace. These videos will help train AI systems to better understand how people complete real-world tasks.


You do not need experience with AI. We are looking for business owners with active teams and real day-to-day work.


Who can participate

Your business may be a good fit if you:

  1. Are an owner, partner, or co-owner of a business in LATAM, the United States, or Canada
  2. Have at least 2 employees who can participate
  3. Have regular work activities that can be recorded safely
  4. Can have each participating employee record at least 10 hours of work
  5. Can get permission to record in the workplace
  6. Can make sure participating employees agree to be recorded
  7. Can start soon after a short onboarding call
  8. Employees will use their own iPhone or Android phone to record. Their phone must have an ultra-wide camera and the required motion sensors.


Businesses that may be a good fit

Examples include:

  1. Construction, HVAC, plumbing, electrical, painting, and renovation businesses
  2. Auto repair, equipment repair, and maintenance businesses
  3. Machine shops, fabrication shops, woodworking, and manufacturing businesses
  4. Warehouses, logistics, delivery, and fulfillment businesses
  5. Landscaping, cleaning, pest control, and property maintenance businesses
  6. Catering companies, bakeries, restaurants, and commercial kitchens
  7. Hardware stores, garden centers, greenhouses, and nurseries
  8. The best fit is a business where employees do different hands-on tasks throughout the day. Assembly-line or highly repetitive work is not a fit.


Privacy and consent

We take privacy seriously. Before recording starts, the business owner must make sure employees agree to participate and that the business has permission to record.

Participants should not record any sensitive information.


Payment

Businesses are paid based on the amount and quality of approved video data collected.


Requirements

  1. You own or help run a business in LATAM, the United States, or Canada
  2. You have at least 2 employees who can participate
  3. Each employee can record at least 10 hours weekly
